title: [FLINK-41068][table] Don't store build rows whose join key can never match in LATERAL SNAPSHOT joins
body:
## What is the purpose of the change

`LateralSnapshotJoinOperator` stored build rows whose join key has a NULL in a field that isn't null-safe. Such rows can never match. Unlike in the window and interval joins, nothing bounds this state except state TTL: a row stays until the build side retracts it, or until TTL removes it if TTL is configured. All such rows share one key, so they pile up in a single subtask, and every probe with a NULL key scans all of them. This is the follow-up to FLINK-41034 for this operator.

## Brief change log

- `processElement2` doesn't buffer an INSERT or UPDATE_AFTER build change when `JoinConditionWithNullFilters#currentKeyCannotMatch` is true. The build side is never preserved, so the output doesn't change. The idle-flip timer is still armed first, because any build record counts as a build-side signal.
- Retractions are still buffered and applied, so a row that an earlier version stored is removed.
- `applyBuildChanges` doesn't count a retraction of such a row in `numUnmatchedBuildRetractions` when it finds nothing. Otherwise the metric would count every NULL-key delete. The metric's description in the docs (English and Chinese) says so. Non-NULL keys are counted as before.
- The probe side doesn't change. A NULL-key probe now scans an empty build table for its key.

## Verifying this change

This change added tests:

- `LateralSnapshotJoinOperatorTest#joinRespectsNullKeysFilter` now also checks that a NULL-key build row isn't stored, for INNER and LEFT joins. With a null-safe key the row is still stored, which is the positive control.
- `LateralSnapshotJoinOperatorTest#retractsNullKeyBuildRowStoredByEarlierVersion` restores state with a stored NULL-key row, on the heap and RocksDB backends. It checks that the row's retraction still removes it, and that a retraction of a row that was never stored isn't counted in the metric.

The new checks fail if NULL-key rows are stored, if their retractions are dropped too, or if those retractions are counted. The existing LATERAL SNAPSHOT tests pass: the runtime join tests, and the planner plan, semantic, restore and ITCase tests.

No new restore test is needed, because the state layout doesn't change. NULL-key rows stored by an earlier version stay until they are retracted or TTL removes them, as before.

## Does this pull request potentially affect one of the following parts:

- Dependencies (does it add or upgrade a dependency): no
- The public API, i.e., is any changed class annotated with `@Public(Evolving)`: no
- The serializers: no
- The runtime per-record code paths (performance sensitive): yes. It adds one null check per build-side accumulation, and in return it skips buffering and storing rows that can never match.
- Anything that affects deployment or recovery: JobManager (and its components), Checkpointing, Kubernetes/Yarn, ZooKeeper: no
- The S3 file system connector: no

## Documentation

- Does this pull request introduce a new feature? no
- If yes, how is the feature documented? not applicable. The description of `numUnmatchedBuildRetractions` is updated.

 | `avgJoinFanOut` | Gauge | The average number of joined rows emitted per probe-side row. |
 | `numUnmatchedProbeRecords` | Counter | The number of probe-side rows that found no build-side match. For an `INNER JOIN` these produce no output; for a `LEFT JOIN` they are emitted null-padded. |

Retractions of rows whose join key can never match, because a key field that is not compared null-safely is `NULL`, are not counted, since such rows are not stored. |
 
 To diagnose a join that emits no output, check `currentPhase` first. If it is `0` while `numProbeSideRecordsBuffered` keeps growing, the join is stuck in the load phase. 
 Compare `currentBuildSideWatermark` against your `load_completed_time`: if the build-side watermark has stopped advancing below it, the build side has become static or idle and the event-time gate will never be crossed.
